title: Provider capabilities document
description: One self-describing provider document (capabilities/<slug>.json). Additional properties are permitted everywhere except referenceEntry: consumers MUST ignore unknown fields and producers MAY add them within a major.

capabilityNode.description: A recursive capability node. Registry-backed nodes carry key_path + key; vocabulary members omit them. Presence of key is the normative canonical-key discriminator.

providerExclusiveNode.description: A provider-exclusive capability node: the same shape as capabilityNode, but definitionally never a registered canonical key, so it MUST NOT carry key or key_path. The constraint is recursive — every descendant under a provider-exclusive root is itself provider-exclusive.

keyMeta.description: Canonical-key metadata inlined from the key registry at every registry-backed node.

contentTypeNode.description: One content type for a provider. Direct children of capabilities are registry-backed capability nodes.

install_entry_points.description: Where the provider reads this content type on disk: an ordered list of ACIF install-targets rows (ACIF install-targets spec §6). Order is precedence: after filtering by the target OS, the first current row for a scope is the write target.

installEntryPoint.description: One ACIF install-targets row, with ACIF's field names and value spellings. scope, os members, layout and status are open strings for consumers (per the consumer contract, handle an unrecognized value as "unknown/other" for that row, never as a document error); path_template is in ACIF's closed template grammar (§8), and an unrecognized template token follows ACIF install-targets §11.

referenceEntry.description: Source reference, trimmed to {url, verified_at}. additionalProperties is false here — and only here — so pipeline-internal provenance (fetch_method, last_content_hash) can never leak into published output.
